newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -T-bonds must vault 110-10 for more upside.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -T-bonds must vault 110-10 for more upside.

text.p: June T-bonds will struggle to crack a stubborn band of resistance at 110-07 to 110-10 on Friday, technical analysts said.

"The May 2 high of 110-10 is proving very strong," said Mike MacDonald, technical analyst at 4CAST here. "It's also worth noting the 200-day moving average at 110-07 -- so that's quite a strong resistance area."
He said the contract not only had to close above there, but also had to pick up some sustained momentum to allow it to push higher.

By 1024 GMT, the June contract on the new LIFFE/CBOT trading link was at 110-06. The new link enables traders to use open outcry to trade the Bund and T-bond futures on both the Chicago Board of Trade and the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE).

MacDonald at 4CAST said if the contract did clear 110-10, it would come up against more resistance at 110-30 -- the 61.8 percent retracement from the February 18 high at 113-25 to the April 11 low at 106-12.
"At 110-10 the Relative Strength Index was well overbought, so intra-day we're looking for some bearish sentiment," said MacDonald.
He put initial support in the 109-24 area, a previous pivotal area on intra-day charts.
Below that, Friday's low so far at 109-16, then intraday congestion at 109-07 would act as further supports, he said.
"Beneath there, there's stronger support at 108-30, yesterday's low, then 108-12."
Philippe Cahen, technical analyst at Credit Lyonnais in Paris, was more bullish on T-bond futures.
"I think we could go to this level even today," he said. He put major support at 109-25.
By 1044 GMT, September Eurodollars were up 0.070 at 93.915.
